title: Previewing a content-search hit opens at the matching line and highlights it
problem: A Contents search lists one row per file with the first matching line as text, e.g. `42: foo` (src/finder/mod.rs:2992-3028; `Row.detail`, mod.rs:102-103). `content_search` asks the engine for up to 20 hits per file (`per_file: 20`, mod.rs:3003) but throws away all but the first (`seen` set, mod.rs:3007-3012) and keeps only a formatted string. The hit's `line`, `byte_offset` and `ranges` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:223-234) are dropped, although fff-search documents `byte_offset` as usable 'by the preview to seek directly without scanning from the top' (fff-search-0.11.0/src/grep/types.rs:52-54). The preview code never looks at the search: src/finder/preview.rs has no reference to the query or hits; `load_preview` always reads the first 64 KB (`TEXT_LIMIT`, preview.rs:38; `read_text`, preview.rs:284-305) and the Text and Code arms draw it from the top with no mark (preview.rs:985-1033). So selecting a hit on line 900 shows line 1 in the preview pane, the gallery and Quick Look, and the user must hunt for the line by eye. Content search covers files up to 10 MB by default (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:377), so a match beyond the first 64 KB is not in the preview at all.
proposal: 1) mod.rs: add `pub struct ContentHit { line: u64, offset: u64 }` and `hits: Arc<[ContentHit]>` on `Row` (empty for name searches). In `content_search` (mod.rs:3007-3019) push later hits of an already-seen path onto that row instead of `continue`. Add `Finder::content_hits(&self, path) -> Option<Arc<[ContentHit]>>`, valid only while `is_searching() && search_contents`. 2) preview.rs `preview_body`, Text and Code arms: for each hit with `offset < text.len()` on a char boundary, mark `offset..end_of_line` with a `HighlightStyle { background_color }` (theme warning/selection colour at low alpha), merged into the syntax spans with `gpui_kit::combine_highlights` (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/style.rs:990). 3) Jump: replace the `overflow_y_scrollbar()` wrapper in these two arms with an explicit scroll area as src/finder/pdf.rs:679-688 does (`div().id(..).overflow_y_scroll().track_scroll(&handle)` inside a `relative` parent with `.vertical_scrollbar(&handle)`), the handle held per surface on `Finder` and replaced when the previewed path changes. Split the text into two children at the line start two lines above the first hit (clip/shift the spans at that byte) and call `handle.scroll_to_top_of_item(1)` once per (path, search generation). 4) Second step, same change if time allows: when the first hit's offset is >= TEXT_LIMIT, have `load_preview` take an optional anchor and read a 64 KB window starting at a line boundary shortly before it (seek, skip to next newline), key the cached preview by (path, window start), and show '... earlier lines not shown' above the text. 5) Caption: add 'N matching lines' to `info_line` (preview.rs:840-861) when hits exist. Update docs/manual.md (Searching, Previews) and CHANGELOG.md.
original_test_plan: Unit tests in preview.rs for the pure helpers: `mark_ranges(text, hits)` returns the byte range of each hit line and skips offsets past the end or off a char boundary; `split_spans(spans, at)` clips and shifts. Headless UI test (tests/finder.rs): write `log.txt` with 400 numbered lines and `needle-zebra` on line 300, open the fixture, Cmd+Shift+P for the preview pane, `ui.update(|f,_,cx| { f.set_search_contents(true, cx); f.set_query("needle-zebra".into(), true, cx) })`, `ui.select("log.txt")`; assert a `#[doc(hidden)]` accessor returns the expected marked range, and that the marked child (given `.id("preview-match").test_support()`) has bounds inside `ui.snapshot("preview-pane").bounds()`, i.e. it was scrolled into view. Repeat with Quick Look via `ui.in_quick_look`. For step 4, a file with the needle past 64 KB still yields a preview containing it.
original_risks: Byte offsets only line up when the previewed text is byte-identical to the file; `read_text` decodes lossily (preview.rs:301), so guard with `is_char_boundary` and skip marks that fail. The engine trims `text` (`trim: true`, mod.rs:3004), so highlight whole lines rather than trusting `ranges`. Mid-file windows start syntect without earlier state, so colours can be off for the first lines (or leave such windows plain). `Row` grows by one Arc pointer. Conflicts with the `per_file: 1` change in search-truncation-honesty: keeping later hits per file needs per_file > 1 with a file-based page, so decide the two together. Replacing the scroll wrappers also resolves preview-scroll-per-file and overlaps step 4 of preview-page-keys.

verifier.claim_check:
The described behaviour is true; I could not refute it.

- **Hits are discarded.** `content_search` (src/finder/mod.rs:2992-3028) asks for `per_file: 20` (3003), drops every later hit of a path through the `seen` set (3007-3012) and keeps only `format!("{}: {}", hit.line, hit.text.trim())` as `Row.detail` (3014-3015; field at 102-103).
- **The engine already supplies what is needed.** `GrepHit` carries `line`, `byte_offset` and `ranges` (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:223-234, filled at 975-988). fff-search documents `byte_offset` as the absolute offset of the matched line, "used by the preview to seek" (fff-search-0.11.0/src/grep/types.rs:52-54; taken from grep-searcher in sink.rs:54-55).
- **The preview ignores the search.** src/finder/preview.rs has no reference to the query, search or hits (grep is empty, also for quick_look.rs and preview_pane.rs). `read_text` reads the first 64 KB (`TEXT_LIMIT` at 38, function at 284-305). The Text arm draws `.child(text)` and the Code arm draws `StyledText` from the top, both inside `overflow_y_scrollbar()` (985-1033). `info_line` (840-861) has no match information.
- **Default file size limit.** `max_file_size_mb: 10` (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:377).
- **Docs and tests.** docs/manual.md:335 says "Results show the first matching line" and :401 says "The first 64 KB"; nothing says the preview follows the match, and CHANGELOG.md has nothing on it. No test pins the current behaviour: tests only toggle `by-contents` (tests/controls.rs:371-376), and no test references `text-preview` or `code-preview`.

Errors in the proposal:
1. **Wrong pattern citation.** src/finder/pdf.rs:679-688 tracks a `v_virtual_list`, not `div().overflow_y_scroll().track_scroll()`. The div pattern with `scroll_to_item` is at src/finder/views.rs:1054-1057 with src/finder/mod.rs:2918, and src/finder/sidebar.rs:403-408.
2. **Jump key.** "Once per (path, search generation)" would yank the scroll repeatedly. `search_gen` is bumped by every `run_search` (mod.rs:1364), which has about 15 callers, including the automatic retry roughly every 600 ms while indexing (1435-1457) and the index-finished re-run (1510).
3. **Surfaces.** There are three, not two: the preview-pane card (`render_preview_card`, preview.rs:768-838, which calls `preview_body` with no surface), the gallery and Quick Look. `pdf::Surface` has only Gallery and QuickLook and indexes `[Shown; 2]`. `preview_body` takes `&Finder` (864-870), so it cannot record "scrolled once" itself.
4. **Test assertion.** The proposed `preview-match` child runs from the split to the end of the text, so it is taller than the pane and can never have "bounds inside" it.
5. **Caption.** "N matching lines" would undercount: `per_file` caps hits at 20 and the engine truncates at `limit` (engine.rs:989).
6. **Markdown.** `.md` files render through `TextView::markdown` (preview.rs:928-941), so they get neither mark nor jump. The proposal does not mention this.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Do steps 1-3 in corrected form, drop steps 4 and 5. All paths are under the repository root.

**1. Data (src/finder/mod.rs)**
- Do not add an `Arc` to every `Row`; an empty `Arc<[T]>` allocates per row on large folder listings. Keep `content_hits: HashMap<PathBuf, Arc<[u64]>>` on `Finder`, holding 1-based line numbers.
- Build it in `content_search` (2993-3028): instead of `continue` at 3010-3012, push `hit.line` onto the entry for that path. Return it beside the rows.
- Install it where `this.results = rows` is set (1428); the name-search branch installs an empty map.
- Add `pub(super) fn content_hits(&self, path: &Path) -> Option<&Arc<[u64]>>`, gated on `self.is_searching() && self.search_contents`, because `results` goes stale after a toggle.
- Use line numbers, not `byte_offset`. `read_text` decodes lossily (preview.rs:301) and `.nu` previews pass through `nu-highlight` and `ansi::parse` (171-173), so bytes can shift but newlines do not. Slicing at line starts is always on a char boundary, which `StyledText::with_highlights` debug-asserts (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/text.rs:444-447).

**2. Pure helpers (src/finder/preview.rs)**
- `mark_ranges(text: &str, lines: &[u64]) -> Vec<Range<usize>>`: one pass over the newlines, returning each hit line without its `\n`; skip lines past the end of the loaded text.
- `split_spans(spans, at) -> (before, after)`: clip spans that cross the split and shift the tail.

**3. Drawing (`preview_body`, Text arm 985-1002 and Code arm 1003-1033)**
- The Text arm must change from `.child(text)` to `StyledText`.
- Merge marks with the existing spans via `gpui_kit::combine_highlights` (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/style.rs:990). Its output is sorted and non-overlapping.
- Mark with `HighlightStyle { background_color: Some(..), ..Default::default() }`.

**4. Scroll area**
- Give `preview_body` a surface argument: a private `enum TextSurface { Card, Gallery, QuickLook }` in preview.rs, with `preview_scroll: [ScrollHandle; 3]` on `Finder`. Do not extend `pdf::Surface`.
- Replace `overflow_y_scrollbar()` in the two arms with a `relative` wrapper carrying `.vertical_scrollbar(&handle)` around `div().id(..).size_full().p(ui(12.)).overflow_y_scroll().track_scroll(&handle)`.
- The tracked div's direct children are: text before the split, text from the split (`id("preview-match").test_support()`), then the truncated note.
- Split at the line start two lines above the first mark. Drop the `\n` that ends the first part, or a blank line appears.
- Optionally wrap the area in `gpui_kit::base::ScrollBounce::new` (public, gpui-base-0.8.1/src/scroll_bounce.rs:154) to keep the macOS bounce that `Scrollable` provides (gpui-component-0.8.1/src/scroll/scrollable.rs:209-215).

**5. Arming the jump**
- Do it in `selection_changed` (mod.rs:1720), which is `&mut self` and is reached from every selection change and from search completion (1431).
- Keep `preview_jump_key: Option<(PathBuf, Option<u64>)>`, meaning (primary path, first hit line). Only when it changes, replace the three handles with `ScrollHandle::new()` and, if there is a first hit, call `scroll_to_top_of_item(1)` on each.
- Never key on `search_gen`.
- gpui keeps the request pending until a tracked div with that child is prepainted (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/elements/div.rs:4402-4447). It therefore survives `Preview::Loading` and a Quick Look opened later.

**6. Cut from scope**
- **Step 4 (64 KB window around a far match).** It re-keys `previews: HashMap<PathBuf, Preview>`, which is used by `ensure_preview`, `preview_of`, `has_preview_for_test` (mod.rs:707), batch_rename.rs:227 and dialogs.rs:846, and it breaks syntect state mid-file. Instead, when the first hit line is past the loaded text, extend the truncated note: "… (preview truncated; the match on line N is further down)".
- **Step 5 ("N matching lines").** The count is capped by `per_file`, so it would be wrong.

**7. Decisions to make explicitly**
- **Markdown.** Either leave it rendered and say so in the manual, or draw the source through the Text arm while the file has hits.
- **`per_file`.** The jump needs only the first hit, so this change works with `per_file: 1`; extra marks are a bonus of whatever `per_file` stays. Coordinate with the search-truncation-honesty candidate.

**8. Docs**
- docs/manual.md: the Contents row (335) and the "Code and other text" row (401).
- CHANGELOG.md: Unreleased › Added.

The scroll-area change also resets the scroll per file, which overlaps the preview-scroll-per-file and preview-page-keys candidates; land them together.
verifier.test_plan:
**Unit tests** in the existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` of src/finder/preview.rs (next to `previews_by_kind`):
- `mark_ranges`: a hit on line 1, a middle line, and the last partial line; CRLF text; a line number past the end is skipped; multibyte text yields ranges on char boundaries.
- `split_spans`: a span before the split, one after it (shifted), and one crossing it (clipped into both halves).

**Headless UI test** in tests/finder.rs, using tests/common/mod.rs:
- Create `Fixture::new("content-jump")` and write `log.txt` (400 numbered lines, `needle-zebra` on line 300) before `Ui::open`. The engine is built with `watch: false`, so files written later are not indexed.
- Then: `ui.click("view-list")`, `ui.press(&cmd("shift-p"))`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| { f.set_search_contents(true, cx); f.set_query("needle-zebra".into(), true, cx) })`, `ui.select("log.txt")`.
- Assert a new `#[doc(hidden)] preview_marks_for_test(&path)` returns the byte range of line 300.
- Assert the jump with `let pane = ui.snapshot("preview-pane").bounds(); let m = ui.snapshot("preview-match");` then `m.visible()` and `m.bounds().top() >= pane.top() && m.bounds().top() < pane.bottom()`. Check the top edge only, because the child is taller than the pane.
- Re-run the same query with `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.run_search(false, cx))` after `ui.scroll(..)` and assert the offset did not snap back.
- Select `notes.txt` and assert `!ui.exists("preview-match")`.
- Repeat the jump assertion in Quick Look: `ui.press("space")`, then `ui.in_quick_look(|ui| ui.snapshot("preview-match"))`.
- Add a `main.rs` fixture with the needle to cover the Code arm.
- Far match: a file whose only hit is past 64 KB shows no `preview-match`, and the truncated note names the line.

The headless platform uses `NoopTextSystem`, but text height is line-height times lines, so the 400-line text overflows the 240 px card and the scroll is observable. I did not run cargo, as instructed.
verifier.risks:
- **All text and code previews change, not only search hits.** Replacing `overflow_y_scrollbar()` loses `Scrollable`'s macOS bounce and axis lock unless `ScrollBounce` is re-wrapped. Scroll position now resets per file, which is an improvement but a visible change.
- **Scroll yanking.** If the jump is keyed on anything that changes on a search re-run, the preview snaps back while the user reads; the indexing retry loop makes this very visible.
- **Stale previews.** The cache is keyed by path only and cleared only on refresh or theme change. A file edited after it was previewed can get its mark on the wrong line. This staleness exists today; a cheap guard is to compare the marked line's trimmed start with the hit text.
- **Per-frame cost.** `preview_of` already clones the spans every frame; the split adds two string copies of up to 64 KB per frame while a file has hits. This is acceptable, or cache the split when the preview loads.
- **Markdown hits** get no jump unless the source-text fallback is chosen.
- **Matches past 64 KB** stay unseen; the note only names the line.
- **`per_file` trade-off.** With `per_file: 20` and a page of `limit * 4` hits, a common word can fill the page with as few as `limit / 5` files, so keeping extra marks competes with file coverage.
- **Effort** becomes L if the 64 KB window (step 4) is kept in scope.

orchestrator_notes: 'preview-scroll-per-file' (a text or code preview opens scrolled to where the previous file's preview was left) lands right before this one in the same lane. Build on what it did instead of redoing it.
